review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the Selector.MassFamily and meanColor definitions, roundingMass, colorLaw and its @[simp] colorLaw_weight lemma, and FiniteLaw.expectation. The file has no simp attributes of its own. The only simp-interface issue I found is that fractionalMassFamily has no projection lemma. The `change` that unfolds the expectation in `hmean` is a similar but weaker point, so I did not report it. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemma is untested.

findings.declaration: fractionalMassFamily (and its use in hlower of fractionalCover_rounding)
findings.problem: fractionalMassFamily is a new structure-valued definition with no simp or rfl projection lemma for its `weight` field. Consumers must unfold the definition by name, as in `simpa only [Selector.meanColor, mu, fractionalMassFamily, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using hH`. That call also unfolds the local `let mu` and ties the proof to the definition's internal shape. The sibling `colorLaw` has the matching simp lemma `colorLaw_weight`, so this definition breaks the project's own convention. Any other client that needs `(fractionalMassFamily ..).weight H x` has to repeat the unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma directly after the definition: `@[simp] theorem fractionalMassFamily_weight (F g hr hcover hcost) (H : ↥F) (x : α) : (fractionalMassFamily F g hr hcover hcost).weight H x = roundingMass g H.val x := rfl`. Then `hlower` can use `simpa only [Selector.meanColor, mu, fractionalMassFamily_weight, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using hH` and no longer unfolds the definition. The normal form is the plain `roundingMass g H.val x`, which is the form that the lemmas `memberMass_ge_half` and `productScore_lower_of_mean` use. The rewrite is safe because the left side is a field projection of a definition, so it cannot loop.
findings.benefit: Callers get a canonical simp normal form for the mass family. The proof no longer depends on how the definition is built. The pattern matches the existing `colorLaw_weight` convention, and `simp` can reach `roundingMass` directly in later lemmas.
